close_reason: Added depth-cap consumer-contract rustdoc to validate_metadata_filter at metadata.rs:617-636. Cross-references the foundation-level epic JMAP-xmvz which tracks the proper architectural fix (workspace-shared depth-capped walker helper in jmap-server). Documentation-only; cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings clean; cargo doc --no-deps --all-features clean with -D warnings.
description:
Section C — untrusted-input boundary, defense-in-depth gap. The two filter walkers in `crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/metadata.rs` recurse unboundedly on attacker-controlled filter trees:

- `walk_filter_for_unknown_keys(node: &Value)` at metadata.rs:656 — recurses on every `conditions[]` child of an operator node (Value tree).
- `walk_filter_for_related_ids_constraint(filter: &Filter<MetadataFilterCondition>)` at metadata.rs:697 — recurses on every `op.conditions` child (typed tree).

Both functions run after `serde_json::from_slice` has produced the request body, and `serde_json`'s default 128-level deserializer recursion cap therefore bounds the worst-case depth. `crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:42-47` further documents that HTTP integrators SHOULD reject bodies with more than ~32 levels of JSON nesting. So in the kit's intended deployment posture this is **not exploitable** — by the time control reaches these walkers, depth is already capped.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: an integrator who skips the HTTP-layer depth cap (the disclosure is in jmap-server's rustdoc, not enforced at the type level) ships a process where a malicious `/query` call with a 128-deep `Filter::Operator` tree triggers ~128 stack frames per walker × 2 walkers = ~256 frames of recursion in this code path before the request even reaches the backend. Rust's default 8 MiB thread stack absorbs this, but a tokio worker on a smaller stack (e.g. `Runtime::worker_stack_size` tuned down for an embedded deployment) would not.

Why this is filed as defense-in-depth (P3), not P1:

- The kit explicitly documents the depth-cap responsibility on the consumer side (jmap-server parse.rs:42-47).
- The 32-level recommendation is well above any legitimate JMAP filter shape (operator-nesting of 3-4 is the realistic upper bound in observed JMAP traffic).
- No actual stack-overflow demonstration exists; this is a 'what if the consumer skips the cap' finding.

Mitigation (one of):
1. Document on `validate_metadata_filter` and the two walker functions that 'the caller MUST ensure the filter tree depth is bounded; this code does not enforce its own cap.' Cross-link to jmap-server parse.rs depth notes.
2. Add an internal walker-side counter (constant: 32 to match the jmap-server recommendation) that returns `unsupportedFilter` with a 'filter nesting exceeds server limit' description on overflow. Symmetric with the MergePatch `DepthExceeded` pattern at memory.rs:1013-1025.
3. Both — defense-in-depth in the same spirit as the workspace's `apply_jmap_patch` depth cap (bd:JMAP-wlip.1).

Canonical-template note: `jmap-mail-server` should be reviewed for the same pattern in `EmailFilterCondition` walkers before propagating this fix here. Per workspace AGENTS.md propagation rule, fix canonical first, then sweep siblings.

Refs:
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/metadata.rs:656 (walk_filter_for_unknown_keys)
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/metadata.rs:697 (walk_filter_for_related_ids_constraint)
- crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:42-47 (depth-cap consumer contract)
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/memory.rs:1013-1025 (MergePatch DepthExceeded — symmetric precedent)
title: Filter walkers recurse on attacker-controlled JSON without explicit depth cap (defense-in-depth)
